predictions.reason: Pregnancy does not alter the fundamental principle that chronic cough requires diagnosis before targeted treatment.
The recommendation to seek professional medical evaluation remains the standard of care and is unchanged by pregnancy status.

proposed_induced: Explicitly avoids recommending medications with known or suspected teratogenic risk or insufficient first-trimester safety data (e.g., codeine, combination cold products) and prioritizes non-pharmacological management or pregnancy-safe alternatives.
Advises deferring or avoiding routine diagnostic imaging (e.g., chest X-ray/CT) due to fetal radiation risks during organogenesis, unless clinically urgent.
Recommends coordinating with an obstetric provider before starting any new treatment due to critical first-trimester fetal development.

Mentions pregnancy-specific warning signs (e.g., vaginal bleeding, severe pelvic pain, dizziness) that require immediate obstetric evaluation, as severe coughing can exacerbate pregnancy complications.
